audit_findings.title: The anchor may perpetuate a nonrecurring litigation charge
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $11.3 million charge, equal to 47.5% of the $23.8 million anchor; computed full-add-back sensitivity before tax and liability adjustments is approximately $2.30-$3.22 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The charge affects the OE anchor if treated as recurring; if normalized out of OE, the accrued judgment must instead enter the equity bridge until paid or reversed
audit_findings.evidence: We recognized expenses of $11.3 million stemming from an employee litigation matter (refer to Note 14, Legal Proceedings and Contingencies, in our Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for details).
audit_findings.explanation: The litigation expense and reserve are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the OE worksheet normalized them. Perpetuating the charge would materially understate earnings power, while adding it back without recognizing the unpaid obligation would overstate equity value. Its scale relative to the anchor makes the treatment capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE worksheet, determine the cash and tax treatment of the $11.3 million reserve, and rerun all scenarios with the charge counted exactly once—either retained in OE or normalized from OE with the remaining liability deducted from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to omit an unfunded pension claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $9.0 million deficit at December 31, 2025; computed dollar-for-dollar effect is approximately $0.15 per share and 1.4%-1.6% of scenario equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The funded-status deficit is a senior liability that would reduce the equity bridge independently of recurring pension expense in OE
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the projected benefit obligation was $23.2 million, the plan assets were $14.2 million and the net pension liability was $9.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 filing demonstrates a $9.0 million unfunded liability and the stated bridge contains no explicit pension adjustment. Nevertheless, even a full dollar-for-dollar deduction is only about $0.15 per share versus scenario values of $9.36-$11.27 and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 30, 2026 funded status and whether an equivalent adjustment exists elsewhere; if not, deduct the applicable after-tax deficit in the next bridge rerun.

audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor predates a material restructuring
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $6.569 million of first-half 2026 restructuring-related charges, equal to 27.6% of the $23.8 million anchor; this included $4.742 million of severance and other charges and $1.827 million of stock-based compensation
audit_findings.mechanism: The restructuring changes normalized OE through one-time cash costs, noncash compensation and any demonstrated recurring payroll savings
audit_findings.evidence: On January 31, 2026, the Company approved a reduction in force that resulted in the termination of approximately 7% of the Company’s global workforce on February 2, 2026 in order to decrease the Company’s costs and create a more efficient organization to support its business.
audit_findings.explanation: The stale cost base is demonstrated: the valuation uses FY2025 OE even though the 7% workforce reduction was substantially completed in Q1 2026. The filed restructuring charge is large relative to the anchor, but the sustainable savings are not isolated because expenses also changed for reclassifications and other operating factors. Excluding the costs overstates value; ignoring durable savings understates it.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct owner earnings through June 30, 2026, count the $4.539 million cash payments and $0.203 million remaining restructuring liability exactly once, exclude nonrecurring stock compensation consistently, and rerun using only recurring savings supported by post-restructuring payroll and departmental expense evidence.

audit_findings.title: Patent litigation could create an unreserved senior claim or impair operating earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: A damages claim, royalty or product restriction would have affected the bridge or future OE, but the filed settlement eliminated those channels
audit_findings.evidence: Currently, the Company is not able to estimate a loss or a range of loss for the ongoing litigations disclosed above.
audit_findings.explanation: This was an unresolved possibility in the 2025 filing, but the June 2026 filing states that the dispute was settled in April 2026 without payment, with a full release, covenant not to sue the company or its customers, dismissal of the appeal and closure of the matter. No valuation adjustment remains for this litigation.
audit_findings.action: Retain the April 2026 settlement disclosure in the audit record; no valuation rerun is needed for this finding.

audit_findings.title: Inventory reserve judgment could overstate the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed inventory was $166.887 million at December 31, 2025 and $157.790 million at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: An inadequate obsolescence provision would overstate gross profit and OE when inventory is sold or written down, potentially also affecting forecast margins and working capital
audit_findings.evidence: We identified the determination of excess and obsolete inventories within work-in-process and finished goods inventories as a critical audit matter due to the significant assumptions made by management when determining the excess and obsolete inventory quantities and the resulting provision.
audit_findings.explanation: The critical-audit-matter disclosure establishes estimation risk, not an inadequate reserve or misstatement. Historical write-downs were reported as immaterial and inventory declined by $9.097 million during the first half of 2026, but the supplied record lacks aging, sell-through and reserve data needed to determine whether the remaining exposure is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain reserve balances and inventory aging by product, compare forecasts with 2026 sell-through, review distributor inventory and subsequent write-downs or concessions, and rerun OE only for a demonstrated reserve shortfall.

audit_findings.title: Discrete tax benefits may be embedded in sustainable OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $1.281 million gross 2025 statute-of-limitations release; its income-statement and OE effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring tax releases or an abnormally low cash tax rate increase after-tax OE and are perpetuated when latest-actual OE is grown
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, in 2025 and 2024, our effective tax rate was favorably impacted by discrete items associated with the release of unrecognized tax benefits caused by an expiration in the statute of limitations on these positions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a discrete tax-position release and a negative 5.3% effective tax rate in 2025, while the first half of 2026 effective rate was 13.3%. However, valuation OE may use cash-tax adjustments, and the filing does not isolate how much of the gross release entered the $23.8 million anchor or establish a sustainable operating cash-tax rate. The direction is adverse, but materiality cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE tax line to 2025 cash taxes, deferred taxes, credits and uncertain-tax-position releases; establish a recurring operating cash-tax rate incorporating 2026 rules, then rerun all scenarios without discrete benefits.
